required_acquisition_relations.semantics: Item is sold by an NPC/shop; depends on NPC script, shop implementation, price, and eligibility conditions.
Item is directly or pool-conditionally dropped by a mob; depends on mob/template/loot source and pool semantics.
Item is synthesis output; depends on recipe, craft/skill requirements, key items, crystal, ingredient identities, and crafting runtime.
Item is granted by quest/instance/event/ANNM content; depends on the rewarding content's completion/reward logic.
Synthesis recipe consumes an ingredient item.
Acquisition or recipe requires a key item/unlock.
Multiple independently valid ways to obtain the same logical item; each path can be scoped independently.

package_scope_rules: Core item/behavior implementation and acquisition are separate review dimensions.
Selecting one acquisition path must not automatically include every alternate acquisition path.
Selecting synthesis must recursively expose recipe prerequisites and ingredient items.
Selecting a quest/instance reward must recursively expose that content's reward/completion dependencies.
A missing recipe/reward edge in server source must remain visible as EXTERNAL_EVIDENCE or IMPLEMENTATION_GAP rather than being silently treated as absent.
Drop pools must preserve one_of/pool semantics rather than flattening every pool member into an always-drop relation.
If the target already has an equivalent acquisition path, it may be classified TARGET_EQUIVALENT independently of core item behavior.
known_toolkit_gaps: No generic acquisition graph currently distinguishes shop, drop, synthesis, quest/instance reward, exchange, or event reward.
No synthesis recipe logical model currently links outputs to craft/key-item/crystal/ingredient prerequisites.
No generic reward-edge analyzer currently links mission/quest/instance completion to rewarded item identities.
No first-class representation currently preserves one_of loot-pool semantics as conditional acquisition evidence.
External retail evidence cannot currently be reconciled against missing/incomplete server implementations as a package-scope finding.
Acquisition paths are not currently independently selectable from core feature behavior in the package manifest.
